aspects.fertilizer:
**General Soil and Fertilizer Advice:**
Determine per-acre fertilizer quantities based on laboratory soil tests.
Apply recommended fertilizer rates for average fertility soils.
For private company seeds, apply fertilizers according to their recommended rates.
Balanced fertilizer use protects the crop from climate change impacts and ensures better yield.
Contact the nearest government soil and water testing laboratory for more information.

**Cholistan Raya, Super Raya, AARI Canola, Sarson DGL, and Canzola:**
Nutrient requirement is 35 kg nitrogen, 30 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potash per acre.
First combination option is 1.25 bags DAP and 0.5 bag SOP at sowing.
Second combination option is 3.25 bags SSP 18 percent, 0.5 bag Urea, and 0.5 bag SOP.
Third combination option is 1 bag Nitrophos, 2.25 bags SSP 18 percent, and 0.5 bag SOP.

**Barani Star, Chakwal Raya, and Barani Sarson:**
Nutrient requirement is 35 kg nitrogen, 23 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potash per acre.
First combination option is 1 bag DAP and 0.5 bag SOP at sowing.
Second combination option is 2.5 bags SSP 18 percent, 0.5 bag Urea, and 0.5 bag SOP.
Third combination option is 1 bag Nitrophos, 1.5 bags SSP 18 percent, and 0.5 bag SOP.

**Rain-fed Barani Areas:**
Apply the full dose of all fertilizers at sowing time.

**Irrigated Areas:**
Apply all phosphorus and potash fertilizers at sowing.
Apply one-third of the total nitrogen fertilizer at sowing.
Split the remaining nitrogen fertilizer into two equal parts.
Apply the first half with the first irrigation.
Apply the second half before flowering.

**Nutrient Adjustments and Substitutions:**
Apply 4 to 5 kg sulfur per acre with the second irrigation to improve yield and quality.
Use Ammonium Sulphate instead of Urea if it is available.
Apply Boron to enhance flowering and pollination.
If SOP is not available, MOP can be used instead, but it must be applied with 2 kg sulfur per acre.

**Punjab Khad Hisab App:**
Soil Fertility Research Institute Punjab Lahore developed a free mobile app named Khad Hisab, available on the Google Play Store.
The app calculates balanced fertilizer requirements for mustard and other crops, whether a soil analysis report is available or not.
Farmers can watch the short instructional video in the app introduction section to learn how to use it.
aspects.harvesting:
**Toria-A Variety:**
Toria-A mustard matures in 90 to 100 days.
Its seed contains 44 percent oil.
Its typical yield is 10 to 12 maunds per acre.
It requires insects for pollination, and yield decreases if insect numbers decline during flowering.
It is commonly cultivated for saag.

**All Punjab Varieties:**
UAF-11 mustard is sown from September 1 to October 15, and harvested from January 1 to February 15.
Barani Star, Chakwal Sarson, and Barani Sarson are sown from September 15 to October 15, and harvested from March 15 to April 15.
Barani Star, Chakwal Sarson, and Barani Sarson are suitable for loam or light loam soil.
Sarson DGL and Rohi Sarson are sown from October 1 to October 31, and harvested in March.

**Harvesting Signs:**
Timely harvesting is essential for good yield and quality.
Harvesting immature crops results in weak seeds and low oil content.
Over-mature harvesting causes pods to shatter, seeds to drop, and yield loss.
Harvest when leaves turn yellow, seeds turn reddish, and 70 percent of pods turn brown in mustard and canola, or 80 percent in raya.

**Combine Harvesting:**
A combine harvester is recommended for large crop areas.
Harvest with a combine harvester when 90 percent or more pods turn brown.
Properly adjust and replace the combine harvester sieve.
Maintain 90,000 plants per acre for mustard, raya, or canola if harvesting by combine harvester.

**Storage and Pest Control:**
Ensure mustard is thoroughly dry before storage.
Seed moisture content must not exceed 8 percent.
Properly dried seed makes a cracking sound when bitten with teeth.
Excess moisture creates a risk of fungus attack.
Do not mix different varieties during storage.
Inspect godowns regularly for insect attacks.
Fumigate storage by applying 30 to 35 tablets of aluminum phosphide per 1000 cubic feet.

**Domestic Oil Purification:**
Purifying mustard oil at home provides cheap, impurity-free, nutritious cooking oil.
First extract raw oil using a kohlu or expeller.
Heat 5 kilograms of raw mustard oil in a pot or pan up to 85 degrees Celsius.
Do not let the oil boil, but heat it so the vessel cannot be touched.
Add 150 grams of finely ground fuller's earth or gachni to the hot oil.
Stir thoroughly with a spoon for 5 minutes, then remove from the stove.
Make a triangular bag from thick market cloth and hang it from a sturdy stand or charpai.
Filter the lukewarm oil through this bag into a clean vessel.
aspects.irrigation:
Irrigation Schedule:
Three to 4 irrigations are sufficient for mustard, raya, and canola crops.
Apply the first irrigation 25 to 30 days after germination.
Apply the second irrigation at flowering.
Apply the third irrigation in a light quantity near pod formation.

Weather and Ridge Management:
Apply a light irrigation in case of severe frost.
Take special care of irrigation during drought conditions.
Sow the crop on ridges to reduce damage from heavy rains and to easily drain excess water from the field.
Apply water according to crop requirement when cultivated on ridges.

Fertilizer and Pest Control:
Apply balanced chemical fertilizers according to soil fertility for good yield and quality.
Use 4 to 5 kg of sulfur per acre when applying the second irrigation.
Flood 1 liter of Fipronil 5 percent SC per acre with irrigation water to protect mustard from termite attack.

General Crop Care:
Sow the crop at the recommended time for better management.
Pay special attention to plant protection.
Stay informed about weather forecasts before sowing or when irrigating.
aspects.machinery:
Ridge Planting Machinery:
Broadcast seed and fertilizer after land preparation for ridge planting of mustard.
Run a plow and plank, then make ridges at a distance of 2.5 feet using a tractor.
A planter named ridger-cum-seeder is available in the market for this planting method.

Combine Harvester:
Using a combine harvester is better if oilseed crops are grown on a large area.
Harvest when 90 percent or more of the pods turn brown.
Change the combine harvester sieve and make suitable adjustments.
Keep a plant population of 90 thousand per acre for canola, raya, or mustard if harvesting with a combine harvester.

Spraying Equipment and Methods:
Fill the machine with plain water before spraying to test it and determine the water volume.
Use the recommended water volume to ensure uniform spray coverage.
Use a flat fan or flood jet nozzle for weed control in mustard.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect pest control.
Do not spray during high winds.
Do not stand against the direction of the wind while spraying.
Avoid repeated use of pesticides from the same chemical group.

Pesticide Waste Disposal:
Bury empty pesticide bottles in the ground.
Dispose of cardboard boxes.
aspects.other:
Greens harvesting:
Plucking greens from the mustard crop increases the risk of aphid attack.
Plucking greens reduces crop yield.
Do not pluck greens from mustard crops grown for seed production.
Reserve a separate plot for harvesting greens.

Spray equipment and pesticide disposal:
Use a flat fan or flood jet nozzle for weed control in mustard.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect pests.
Bury empty poison bottles underground.
Dispose of cardboard boxes.

Climate change management:
Unexpected rains, excessive rains, or drought from climate change cause harmful effects on mustard.
Sow the crop at the recommended time to protect it from climate change effects.
Maintain plant protection.
Check the weather forecast before sowing or irrigating.

High-rainfall areas:
Mustard must be cultivated on ridges in high-rainfall areas.

Training programs:
Training programs for mustard are organized at the district and tehsil levels.
Agricultural experts introduce modern cultivation technology to farmers and agriculture department extension staff.
aspects.overview:
Punjab Mustard Statistics:
In 2020-21, mustard area was 413.50 thousand acres (167.34 thousand hectares), total production was 267.26 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 16.16 maunds per acre.
In 2021-22, mustard area was 585.50 thousand acres (236.94 thousand hectares), total production was 403.00 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 17.21 maunds per acre.
In 2022-23, mustard area was 1055.10 thousand acres (426.98 thousand hectares), total production was 665.71 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 15.77 maunds per acre.
In 2023-24, mustard area was 605.20 thousand acres (244.91 thousand hectares), total production was 314.47 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 12.99 maunds per acre.
In 2024-25 provisional estimates, mustard area was 820.65 thousand acres (332.10 thousand hectares), total production was 499.94 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 15.23 maunds per acre.

Mustard Varieties:
Barani Star was developed by Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal for rain-fed areas. It resists drought, insects, and diseases. It yields up to 42 maunds per acre and has up to 42 percent seed oil.
Barani Sarson was developed by Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal. It resists drought, insects, and diseases. It yields up to 34 maunds per acre and has up to 44 percent seed oil.
Toria-A matures in 90 to 100 days and is commonly grown for saag. It yields 10 to 12 maunds per acre and has 44 percent seed oil. It requires insect pollination, so yield drops if insect counts decline during flowering.
Sarson D.G.L is a Gobhi Sarson variety with dark green leaves and thick, soft branches grown for saag and livestock fodder. It yields 10 to 15 maunds of seed per acre after picking saag, with 40 to 42 percent seed oil.
UAF-11 is a short-duration desi mustard developed by University of Agriculture Faisalabad. It has thick, shattering-resistant pods and up to 50 percent oil. Due to high erucic acid, it is used for industrial purposes rather than edible oil. It is suitable for intercropping in sugarcane.

Soil and Cultivation:
Well-drained medium to heavy loam soils are suitable.
Highly saline and waterlogged soils are unsuitable.
In rice zones, clay soils, and high-rainfall areas, sowing on ridges saves water and protects crops.
Adaptive Research Gujranwala trials confirmed good yields by sowing mustard on ridges after rice harvesting.

Rain-fed Areas:
Mustard is sown using moisture conserved from summer rains.
Properly conserving monsoon rainwater increases rabi crop yields by 20 to 25 percent.

Program Management:
The 2025-26 oilseed plan covers canola, mustard, toria, raya, taramira, linseed, and camelina to increase domestic edible oil production and reduce costly imports.
Deputy Directors of Agriculture Extension formulate district strategies, inform the provincial government, and mobilize staff.
Extension staff write guidance and slogans on walls, milestones, and signboards.
The Directorate General of Agricultural Information guides farmers from sowing to harvest through print, electronic, and social media.
aspects.pests_diseases:
Seed Treatment and Storage:
Mustard resists diseases, insects, and shattering. Apply recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kilogram seed. For stem rot, apply 1 gram Thiophanate-methyl per kilogram seed. Do not harvest saag from seed crops. Fumigate warehouses with 30 to 35 aluminum phosphide tablets per 1000 cubic feet.

Termites:
Termites attack underground parts in dry weather. Flood 1 liter Fipronil 5 percent SC per acre with water or apply during rauni.

Rain-fed Areas:
Mix recommended poison in 15 to 20 kilograms fine soil, broadcast before sowing, and plow.

Toka:
Nymphs and adults attack germinating plants, especially near sugarcane, maize, and sorghum. Spray 330 ml Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC or 250 ml Bifenthrin 10 EC per acre.

Mustard Sawfly:
Larvae attack in October and November. Per acre, spray 80 ml Spinetoram 120 SC, 330 ml Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 percent EC, 200 ml Emamectin benzoate 1.9 EC, or 30 grams Fipronil 80 WG.

Painted Bug:
Bugs measure 5 to 7 mm and attack in October and November. Per acre, spray 400 ml Abamectin plus Thiamethoxam 108 SC, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 250 grams Acephate 75 SP, or 250 ml Bifenthrin 10 EC.

Cabbage Butterfly:
Per acre, spray 80 ml Chlorantraniliprole plus Thiamethoxam 300 SC, 80 ml Spinetoram 120 SC, 50 ml Flubendiamide 480 SC, or 250 ml Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC.

Mustard Aphid:
Clusters attack from mid-January to late March. Complete sowing in the first week of October. Per acre, spray 24 grams Thiamethoxam 25 SWG, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 60 grams Flonicamid 50 WG, or 200 ml Clothianidin 20 EC.

Punjab:
Free Chrysoperla cards are available from 11 extension laboratories in Sahiwal, Faisalabad, Hafizabad, Layyah, Vehari, Pakpattan, Sheikhupura, Jhang, Muzaffargarh, Okara, and Toba Tek Singh.

Diseases:
For white rust, spray Propiconazole or Difenoconazole at 1.25 ml per liter water. For epidemic blight at 10 to 25 degrees Celsius during rain, spray Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram or Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter water. For downy mildew, spray Flumorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium at 5 grams or Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil at 6 grams per liter water. For bacterial stem rot during persistent smog, spray 2.5 ml Benzothiazolinone, 1 gram Streptomycin sulphate, or 6 ml Kasugamycin per liter water. For stem rot, spray Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter water. To manage wilt, avoid early sowing, remove weeds, and rotate crops. For plant blight, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 3.5 grams Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin per liter water. For mustard rust, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 2 ml Propiconazole per liter water.

Spray Safety:
Spray only at economic thresholds and in evenings. Use hollow cone nozzles for insects and flat fan or floodjet nozzles for weeds. Wear goggles, gloves, and rubber boots. Do not hoe immediately after spraying.
aspects.sowing:
**Punjab Sowing and Harvesting Dates:**
UAF-11 mustard is sown across all Punjab from 1 September to 15 October and harvested from 1 January to 15 February.
Barani Star, Chakwal Sarson, and Barani Sarson are sown across all Punjab from 15 September to 15 October and harvested from 15 March to 15 April.
Loam or light loam soil is suitable for Barani Star, Chakwal Sarson, and Barani Sarson.
Sarson DGL and Rohi Sarson are sown across all Punjab from 1 October to 31 October and harvested in March.

**Rain-fed (Barani) Areas:**
Deep plow empty fields before the monsoon to conserve rainwater moisture.
Strengthen field bunds, level the land, and plow across the slope as needed.
Do not plow after the rainy season.
Before sowing, plow twice and plank to conserve moisture.
Prepare land in the evening or before sunrise to prevent moisture loss.
Fields must be weed-free and level at sowing time.

**Field Preparation and Row Spacing:**
Prepare the land well and level it with a laser leveler.
Seed depth at sowing must not exceed 1.5 inches.
Keep row spacing at 1.5 feet for Barani Star, Chakwal Raya, Barani Sarson, Khanpur Raya, Sarson DGL, UAF-11, and Super Raya.
Keep row spacing at 1 to 1.5 feet for Canola, Toria, and Tara Mira.

**Ridge Sowing:**
Ridge sowing is recommended in rice areas after paddy harvest, in clay soils, and in high rainfall zones to save water and avoid rain damage.
Broadcast seed and fertilizer after land preparation, run a plow and plank, and make ridges 2.5 feet apart using a tractor.
A ridger-cum-seeder planter is available in the market for this method.
Trials at Adaptive Research Gujranwala confirm good yields from ridge sowing canola, mustard, or raya after harvesting paddy.

**Thinning:**
Thinning must be completed before the first irrigation.
Thin the crop when plants reach the 4-leaf stage.
Remove weak and diseased plants during thinning.
Maintain a distance of 9 to 12 inches between healthy plants.

**Weed Control and Chemical Application:**
If weed infestation is anticipated, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre in 100 liters of water during moderate weather when temperatures are 35 degrees Celsius or lower.
For drill and wattar sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre before the final plowing.
For ridge sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre within 24 hours after sowing.

**Irrigation and Weather Management:**
Pay special attention to irrigation during drought conditions.
Check weather forecasts before sowing and applying irrigation.
aspects.varieties:
Recommended Varieties:
Recommended mustard varieties are Barani Star, Toria-A, Sarson D.G.L., Barani Sarson, and UAF-11.
Other approved oilseed varieties include Cholistan Star, Sandal Canola, Super Canola, Rachna Canola, Khanpur Canola, TM Canola, Chandni for linseed, and RD-73 for taramira.
Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal developed Barani Star and Barani Sarson.
Both varieties resist drought, insects, and diseases.
Barani Star suits rain-fed areas, yielding up to 42 maunds per acre with up to 42 percent seed oil content.
Barani Sarson yields up to 34 maunds per acre with up to 44 percent seed oil content.

Seed Provision:
Limited seed is available from Punjab Seed Corporation, National Agricultural Research Centre Islamabad, Ayub Agricultural Research Institute Faisalabad, Mustard Research Centre Khanpur, Regional Agricultural Research Institute Bahawalpur, and Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal.
Registered private seed companies also sell recommended varieties.
Farmers must use seed certified by the Federal Seed Certification Department.

Punjab Sowing and Soil:
In all Punjab, Barani Star, Chakwal Sarson, and Barani Sarson are sown from 15 September to 15 October.
Harvesting takes place from 15 March to 15 April.
Loam or light loam soil is suitable.
Land must be well prepared and leveled using a laser leveler.
Sowing depth must not exceed 1.5 inches.
Soil must have optimal moisture for good germination.

Seed Rates:
Seed germination must not be less than 80 percent.
For mustard, canola, toria, raya, and taramira, the seed rate is 1.5 to 2 kg per acre in irrigated areas.
Rain-fed areas require 1.5 to 2.5 kg seed per acre.
Cholistan requires 3 to 4 kg seed per acre.
Linseed requires 6 kg seed per acre in irrigated areas and 8 kg per acre in rain-fed areas.

Seed Treatment and Diseases:
Treat seed with recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kg of seed.
Do not increase fungicide quantity and apply correct water, or do not treat if careful dosing is impossible.
Treat seed with Thiophanate-methyl at 1 gram per kg of seed to prevent stem rot.
Spray Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water if stem rot appears.
For downy mildew, spray Flumorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium at 5 grams or Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil at 6 grams per liter of water, use healthy seed, and destroy plant residues.
For blight, use resistant varieties, practice crop rotation, treat seeds, and spray Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram or Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin at 3.5 grams per liter of water.
For wilt, treat seeds with fungicide, avoid early sowing, remove weeds, and rotate crops.

Harvesting:
Use a combine harvester for large acreage.
Harvest when 90 percent or more pods turn brown.
Adjust the harvester screen properly.
Maintain 90,000 plants per acre for mustard, canola, or raya when combine harvesting.
aspects.weeds:
Common Weeds:
Common weeds in mustard include wild oat, canary grass, lashkani booti, bathu, karund, shahtra, and itsit.

Non-Chemical Control:
The daab method is suitable for non-chemical weed control.
In the daab method, plow the field after soaking irrigation or rain when soil is in workable moisture condition, apply heavy planking, and leave the field for 5 to 7 days.
Weeds will germinate and be eliminated during seedbed preparation.
Perform dry hoeing after crop emergence, preferably before rain, to destroy field weeds.
Perform the first hoeing before the first irrigation.
Perform the second hoeing after irrigation once workable moisture condition is reached.
Thin the crop when it reaches four leaves to establish the recommended spacing.
Strictly avoid hoeing immediately after spraying herbicide.
Hoeing right after spraying destroys chemical effectiveness, causes weeds to regrow, and creates airborne chemical dust that harms farmer health through skin contact and inhalation.

Chemical Control:
If high weed infestation is feared, apply recommended chemicals immediately after sowing.
In moderate weather when temperature is 35 degrees Celsius or lower, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor mixed in 100 liters of water per acre immediately after sowing.
For drill and workable moisture sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre before the final plowing.
For ridge sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre within 24 hours after sowing.
Apply pre-emergence herbicide Pendimethalin at 1000 ml per acre.
To eliminate emerged itsit within two weeks of crop emergence, spray 400 to 500 ml Betazachlor 50 percent SC per acre.
Betazachlor spray can be applied without using a shield.

Application Equipment and Safety:
Use a flat fan or floodjet nozzle for weed control sprays.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect pest sprays.
Bury empty chemical bottles underground and destroy cardboard boxes.

Disease Management:
In mustard wilt or collar rot, seeds decay, plants wilt and dry up, and root bark appears split.
To control wilt, treat seed with recommended fungicides before sowing, avoid early sowing, eradicate weeds, and rotate crops.

timing.sowing: 1 September to 31 October, depending on variety
timing.harvesting: January to mid April, depending on variety (UAF-11: 1 January to 15 February; Sarson DGL and Rohi Sarson: March; Barani Star, Chakwal Sarson, Barani Sarson: 15 March to 15 April)
